angle: Black Friday is no longer a day in a store. Over the 2025 Thanksgiving weekend, a record 202.9 million Americans shopped (NRF), and US online spending from Thanksgiving to Cyber Monday reached $44.2 billion in five days (Adobe), with Cyber Monday ($14.25B) bigger than Black Friday ($11.8B) and $1.03 billion of Cyber Monday spending on buy now, pay later. Adobe forecasts $47.5 billion for Cyber Week 2026, about $6.6 million a minute (our calculation).
paragraphs: Last year, from Thanksgiving to Cyber Monday, a record {two hundred and three million|203 million} Americans went shopping.
Online alone, they spent {forty-four billion dollars|$44.2 billion} in five days.
And the biggest day wasn't Black Friday. It was Cyber Monday, at {fourteen billion|$14.25 billion}.
Even more of it is borrowed. On Cyber Monday, {one billion dollars|$1.03 billion} went on buy now, pay later.
This year, Adobe expects {forty-seven and a half billion|$47.5 billion} online. That's about {six and a half million dollars|$6.6 million} every minute.
Black Friday isn't a day anymore. It's a five-day checkout. More on the channel.
